name: Pawmpt
author: qempexe
description: A little pal that lives on your desktop: pick a character or add your own, dress it in skins, and ask it things through an agent you choose.

barWidget.description: Show, hide and set up your desktop pal.

schema.label: Size
schema.description: How big the pal is on the desktop, in pixels.

schema.label: Opacity
schema.description: 100 is solid.

schema.label: Shadow
schema.description: A soft shadow on the ground under it.

schema.label: While idle
schema.description: What it does when you leave it alone. Wobble squashes and stretches like jelly, Twirl turns like a coin, Shiver trembles, Float drifts slowly, Dance rocks side to side, Jumpy leaps now and then, Heartbeat pulses twice and rests, Tilt cocks its head from side to side, Flip does a somersault now and then, Boing bounces and squashes like a rubber ball, Drowsy nods off slowly and jerks awake.

schema.label: Blink
schema.description: Now and then.

schema.label: Eyes follow the mouse
schema.description: It looks at your pointer.

schema.label: Fall asleep after
schema.description: Minutes of quiet before it dozes off. Come near it, click it or ask it something to wake it. 0 never.

schema.label: Surprise me
schema.description: Picks a random character and skin by itself.

schema.label: Start hidden
schema.description: Show it from the bar button or Ask.

schema.label: Moves
schema.description: Bounces goes diagonally and turns at the screen edges, like the DVD logo. Roams picks a random spot on the screen again and again. Circles goes round and round. Rides a wave travels left and right along a sine curve. Patrols walks the edges of the screen. Darts dashes to a spot, pauses, and dashes again. Runs from the mouse keeps away from your pointer. Spirals circles with a radius that grows and shrinks. Figure eight traces an eight. Orbits the mouse circles your pointer. Leaps about jumps in arcs from spot to spot.

schema.label: Speed
schema.description: Pixels per second.

schema.label: Keep away from the edges
schema.description: How far the screen's edges are kept free. Useful for a bar or a dock.

schema.label: Rest now and then
schema.description: Stops for a moment every time it arrives.

schema.label: Rest for about
schema.description: Seconds.

schema.label: Starts going
schema.description: The direction it sets off in.

schema.label: On every bounce
schema.description: Changes it every time it hits an edge. A corner makes it hop.

schema.label: Keeps this far away
schema.description: Pixels between it and the pointer. When it follows, it stops this far away. When it runs from the mouse, it starts running once you are closer than this. When it orbits the mouse, it is the radius of the circle.

schema.label: Face where it goes
schema.description: Turns around when it changes direction.

schema.label: Lean into the move
schema.description: Tilts a little the way it is going.

schema.label: Stop when the mouse is on it
schema.description: So you can click it.

schema.label: Stop while the agent works
schema.description: And while you type a question.

schema.label: Drag it around
schema.description: Hold the left button on it and move.

schema.label: Remember where it was
schema.description: It comes back to the same spot after a restart.

schema.label: Drop it at the side to change screen
schema.description: With several screens: let go at a screen's side edge to send it to the next one.

schema.label: Walk onto other monitors
schema.description: With several monitors: when it reaches the side of a screen it goes on to the monitor next to it, and comes back the same way. Bounces, Left and right, Rides a wave carry on across; Strolls, Roams and Darts about now and then head for the next monitor. On the outer sides it turns round as usual. Monitors are taken in the order they sit from left to right.

schema.label: Agent
schema.description: Who answers. Install the selected agent first. Claude Code and Codex ask in the bubble before they run a command or change a file, and can't read the files that hold keys and passwords.

schema.label: Model
schema.description: Every model your providers offer. Add a provider with opencode auth login, then Refresh.

schema.label: Command
schema.description: Your question goes to it on stdin. It runs without a shell, so no pipes or quotes. {prompt} in it puts the question in the command line instead, where other users on this computer can see it.

schema.label: Approval bridge
schema.description: For a command adapter that speaks Pawmpt's JSONL approval protocol. It receives a request on stdin and may send permission events on stdout; Allow and Deny replies go back on stdin.

schema.label: Thinking effort
schema.description: Only models that think support this; others ignore it.

schema.label: Let it act
schema.description: On, opencode does everything without asking. Off, it reads and searches on its own, and anything else (a command, an edit, the web) waits for Allow once or Deny in the bubble. Keys and passwords stay out of reach either way. These are opencode's own rules, not a sandbox.

schema.label: Look things up online
schema.description: With Let it act off, lets it search the web and open pages without asking first. What it sends there can include what it read.

schema.label: Always tell it
schema.description: A line put in front of every question, for example: Answer in two sentences.

schema.label: Answer style
schema.description: How answers are written. It is added as a line in front of every question, so it works with every agent.

schema.label: Answer in
schema.description: A language for every answer, whatever language you ask in. Empty answers in the language of the question. Translate then translates into it.

schema.label: Remember the conversation
schema.description: Follow-ups continue the same chat until New chat.

schema.label: Start a new chat after
schema.description: Minutes of quiet.

schema.label: Look back on
schema.description: Ollama and your own command have no chat of their own, so the last few questions and answers are sent along with a follow-up. How many exchanges. 0 sends none.

schema.label: Tell it about the active window
schema.description: Adds the window's app, title and folder to your question.

schema.label: Tell it what I have selected
schema.description: Adds the text you have selected, in any app, to your question. It is read only at the moment you ask, and only up to the limit below.

schema.label: Tell it what I copied
schema.description: Adds what is in the clipboard, up to the limit below, to your question.

schema.label: Most text to send
schema.description: Characters taken from the selection or the clipboard, for the quick actions too. More costs more tokens.

schema.label: Work in
schema.description: The active window's folder is where its terminal shell is; other apps fall back to Home.

schema.label: Folder
schema.description: For example ~/Projects/my-app

schema.label: Show quick actions
schema.description: Explain, Summarize, Fix it, Translate, Reply and Shorter, under the question box. Each one works on the text you have selected, or else on what you copied.

schema.label: Your own: name
schema.description: A seventh button of your own. Its name, up to 16 characters. It needs the prompt below too.

schema.label: Your own: what to do
schema.description: What the button asks. The selected or copied text is put after it. From a terminal: quick custom.

schema.label: Copy the answer when it is ready
schema.description: Puts the finished answer on the clipboard, ready to paste. It needs wl-copy (the wl-clipboard package).

schema.label: Notify me when an answer is ready
schema.description: A desktop notification when the agent has finished, for the long ones you walk away from.

schema.label: Only if it took longer than
schema.description: Seconds. A quick answer you were already looking at needs no notification. 0 always notifies.

schema.label: Give up after
schema.description: Seconds.

schema.label: Try again when it fails
schema.description: How many more times to ask when the agent stops with an error, for a provider that now and then drops out. A run you stop, a timeout and a missing agent are not tried again. 0 never.

schema.label: Ask by voice
schema.description: Speak your question. Hex (anoma.ly/hex) is local voice dictation. Pawmpt starts and stops recording; the transcription goes to the question box for review by default. Install and set up Hex first. Then use Ask by voice on a click, the mic in the question box, or: omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt voice.

schema.label: Send when I stop speaking
schema.description: On sends the transcription right away. Off puts it in the question box so you can read and change it before pressing Enter.

schema.label: Stop listening after
schema.description: Seconds. If you forget to stop, Pawmpt ends the recording; the transcription is sent only when Send when I stop speaking is on.

schema.label: Hex command
schema.description: How to run Hex, if it is not on the PATH. ~/.local/bin/hex is looked at when hex is not found.

schema.label: Width
schema.description: Pixels.

schema.label: Text size
schema.description: Pixels.

schema.label: Close after
schema.description: Seconds. 0 keeps the answer until you close it.

schema.label: Show what it is doing
schema.description: The steps while it works: › bash: git status

schema.label: Show tokens and folder
schema.description: The small line under an answer.

schema.label: Follow-up buttons
schema.description: Go on and Simpler, under an answer, to carry on the chat in one click. They show when the conversation is remembered.

schema.label: Colors
schema.description: The colors of this panel and the speech bubble. Follow theme matches your Omarchy theme live. Window borders takes the accent from your theme's window border. Monochrome removes every hue.

schema.label: Background
schema.description: Choose Background, Text or Accent, then pick a swatch or type a hex.

schema.label: Text
schema.description: Choose Background, Text or Accent, then pick a swatch or type a hex.

schema.label: Accent
schema.description: Choose Background, Text or Accent, then pick a swatch or type a hex.

schema.label: Text
schema.description: Always readable keeps your theme's text color and switches to black or white when it would be hard to read.

schema.label: Row style
schema.description: Soft fills the rows lightly, outline draws a border only, flat has neither.

schema.label: Spacing
schema.description: How much air there is between things.

schema.label: Roundness
schema.description: 0 is square, 20 is very round.

schema.label: Text size
schema.description: 1 is normal, 1.25 is a quarter bigger.

schema.label: Panel width
schema.description: How wide the bar panel and the window are.

schema.label: Panel height
schema.description: How tall.

schema.label: Open as
schema.description: Where the bar button opens Pawmpt. You can always pop it out or dock it back from the header.

schema.label: Window outline
schema.description: Draw the edge in your window border's colors instead of a plain neutral line.

schema.label: Outline gradient
schema.description: Use the window border's whole gradient, at its angle, when it has more than one color.

schema.label: Outline color
schema.description: The one color the outline takes when it isn't a gradient.

schema.label: Window tint
schema.description: How much of the accent washes over the background. 0 keeps it plain.

schema.label: Window opacity
schema.description: 100 is solid.

schema.label: Use the theme's colors
schema.description: Body, eyes and details follow your Omarchy theme, live. Picking a color yourself puts the theme's colors in its place to start from.

schema.label: Body
schema.description: Details are the cheeks, ears, belly and so on. Used exactly as you pick them.

schema.label: Eyes
schema.description: Details are the cheeks, ears, belly and so on. Used exactly as you pick them.

schema.label: Details
schema.description: Details are the cheeks, ears, belly and so on. Used exactly as you pick them.

schema.label: Second body
schema.description: The second body color is for the fills below; the outline and the pattern have their own switches.

schema.label: Outline
schema.description: The second body color is for the fills below; the outline and the pattern have their own switches.

schema.label: Pattern
schema.description: The second body color is for the fills below; the outline and the pattern have their own switches.

schema.label: Body fill
schema.description: The two body colors blend.

schema.label: Pattern size
schema.description: Percent.

schema.label: Outline
schema.description: A line around the pal in the outline color. 0 has none.

schema.label: Glow
schema.description: A soft glow around it in the details color.

schema.label: Shine
schema.description: The little white highlight on the body of the round characters. It is not the glow: the glow is the soft light outside the pal, the shine is a spot on it, so you can use both or either.

schema.label: Blush
schema.description: Cheeks, in the details color.
